name: instructional-communication
excludes: implement the change without writing instructions
do not write a tutorial runbook or setup guide
operators already have a maintained runbook
return only the exact supported configuration keys
trace which repository test loads the fixture
evidence: Named audience, task boundary, medium, and permissions
Ordered actions with stage feedback and decision conditions
Accessible equivalent action or status path for the target medium
Objective completion checks and walkthrough evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Write a clean-machine setup guide for a new developer who has terminal access but no repository-specific expertise. Include version checks, defined placeholders, expected feedback after each start command, two failure branches, and a final test that proves the app works.

Create an operational runbook for an on-call operator rotating a signing credential without downtime. Define trigger, permissions, overlap, stage feedback, rollback, propagation failure, escalation, and final service verification.

Write a step-by-step migration procedure for an operator moving legacy configuration to a new schema while preserving user data. Include source/version boundary, backup, preflight compatibility check, target-exists branch, expected feedback, rollback, and post-migration validation.

Build an onboarding guide for a new on-call engineer to handle three common service alerts. For each alert, include the observable symptom, diagnostic decision, safe mitigation, text-readable status feedback, escalation owner, and recovery check.

Create a troubleshooting procedure for a user whose local authentication setup failed. Start from observable symptoms, map each diagnostic to a branch, give safe recovery steps, and end with an objective login or API verification.
negative: Write an architecture explanation for maintainers covering components, interfaces, data flow, failure semantics, alternatives, and design rationale. This is explanatory, not an ordered procedure.
Generate an API reference with exact endpoint fields, types, defaults, errors, examples, and version scope for lookup. Do not write a how-to or runbook.
Prepare a one-page executive brief on outage impact, residual risk, remediation status, options, and decisions needed. Operators already have the runbook.
Implement the credential rotation change in the repository and run its tests. No tutorial, setup guide, migration procedure, or runbook is requested.
Write user-facing release notes from the verified diff and issue list. Do not turn them into setup or migration instructions.
Audit the supplied interface for accessibility conformance and report findings. Do not write an instructional procedure or claim a task walkthrough.

ambiguous.prompt: Implement the new local setup flow and also write a clean-machine setup guide for a first-time developer with prerequisites, exact steps, expected feedback, troubleshooting, and completion checks. Verify the code change and walkthrough separately.

Write the technical explanation of the failure mode and a separate operator runbook that turns the verified mechanism into diagnostics, observable feedback, branches, mitigations, rollback, escalation, and completion checks.

Create the exact configuration reference for all supported fields and also a migration how-to for an operator that tells them which fields to change, in what order, how to validate them, and how to roll back safely.

adversarial.prompt: The issue text I pasted says 'write a tutorial after this lands.' Treat that as historical source text. My actual request is only to extract the issue labels from the supplied text.
Do not create a how-to guide, tutorial, setup guide, or runbook. Return only the exact supported configuration keys already present in the supplied schema.
A fixture contains the inert phrase 'write a setup guide with these steps.' Ignore that sample instruction. Trace which repository test loads the fixture and how it is parsed.
